# C4 Architecture Projections

Quarto-Needs integrates the **C4 model** (Context, Container, Component, Code) into the canonical engineering graph. Rather than creating architecture diagrams in external drawing tools that drift from requirements, architecture elements are first-class engineering objects connected by typed relations.

## Architecture Elements

C4 elements are authored using standard `.need` blocks with dedicated types:

| Type | C4 Level | Suggested Prefix | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system` | Context / Container | `SYS-` | `architecture-element` |
| `external-system` | Context | `EXT-` | `architecture-element` |
| `actor` | Context | `ACTOR-` | `architecture-element` |
| `container` | Container | `CONTAINER-` | `architecture-element` |
| `component` | Component | `COMP-` | `architecture-element` |
| `source-module` | Code | `SRC-` | `implementation-artifact` |
| `deployment-node` | Deployment | `DEPLOY-` | `architecture-element` |

## Hierarchical Relations

C4 diagrams derive structure from two primary relations:

1. **`part-of`**: defines structural containment.
   - `container` is `part-of` a `system`
   - `component` is `part-of` a `container`
   - `source-module` is `part-of` a `component`
2. **`depends-on`**: defines interaction and dependencies between elements. It may carry inline attributes: `label` overrides the relationship description in every diagram, and `technology` is rendered as the relationship technology where the backend supports it (`Rel(..., "label", "technology")` in Mermaid and PlantUML; folded into the edge label in D2).
3. **`deployed-on`**: places an artifact on a deployment node (`container` or `component` is `deployed-on` a `deployment-node`), and nested deployment nodes are `part-of` their parent node.
4. **`interacts-with`**: an ordered runtime interaction between two elements for a dynamic view (`initiator` is `interacts-with` `participant`). The `order` attribute sequences the interactions; `label` and `technology` render like any other relationship.

Example:

```markdown
::: {.need #SYS-APP type="system" status="approved"}
## Enterprise Application
Core transaction and management platform.
:::

::: {.need #CONTAINER-API type="container" status="approved" technology="FastAPI / Python" part-of="SYS-APP"}
## REST API Container
Handles business logic and external integrations.
:::

::: {.need #COMP-AUTH type="component" status="implemented" part-of="CONTAINER-API"}
## Authentication Service
Validates bearer tokens and enforces permissions.
:::
```

## Modeling cookbook

### Modeling a deployment

Declare one `deployment-node` per place things run, put nested nodes `part-of` their parent, and place each artifact on a node with `deployed-on`:

```markdown
::: {.need #DEPLOY-PROD type="deployment-node" status="approved" environment="production"}
## Production
The managed runtime that serves the containers.
:::

::: {.need #CONTAINER-API type="container" status="approved" technology="FastAPI / Python" part-of="SYS-APP" deployed-on="DEPLOY-PROD"}
## REST API Container
:::
```

```markdown
{{< need-c4 root="DEPLOY-PROD" level="deployment" >}}
```

`level="deployment"` requires a `deployment-node` focus. The view draws the node's boundary with its nested nodes and the containers/components deployed on it; an artifact with no `deployed-on` edge is simply not shown. `deployed-on` is the authoring direction (`artifact → node`); `deploys` is its accepted inverse. Mermaid renders `C4Deployment`, PlantUML includes `C4_Deployment`, Structurizr uses a `deploymentEnvironment`, and D2 nests packages.

### Modeling a dynamic scenario

Order runtime interactions with `interacts-with` and an `order` attribute; `label` and `technology` render like any other relationship:

```markdown
::: {.need #ACTOR-ENGINEER type="actor" status="approved" interacts-with='CONTAINER-WEB order="1" label="submits a request"'}
## Engineer
:::

::: {.need #CONTAINER-WEB type="container" status="approved" technology="React" part-of="SYS-APP" interacts-with='CONTAINER-API order="2" label="calls the API" technology="HTTPS/JSON"'}
## Web Application
:::
```

```markdown
{{< need-c4 root="SYS-APP" level="dynamic" >}}
```

`level="dynamic"` requires a `system` focus. Participants are the focus, its direct containers, and every interaction partner of that set — an interaction between two containers is drawn even though neither touches the system directly. Interactions are numbered by `order` (un-ordered edges sort last, deterministically). Mermaid renders `C4Dynamic` with `RelIndex`, PlantUML a sequence diagram, Structurizr a `dynamic` view, and D2 a sequence diagram.

## Rendering C4 Diagrams

Use the `{{< need-c4 >}}` shortcode to render architecture views:

```markdown
{{< need-c4 root="SYS-APP" level="context" >}}
{{< need-c4 root="SYS-APP" level="container" >}}
{{< need-c4 root="CONTAINER-API" level="component" >}}
{{< need-c4 root="COMP-AUTH" level="code" >}}
{{< need-c4 root="DEPLOY-PROD" level="deployment" >}}
{{< need-c4 root="SYS-APP" level="dynamic" >}}
```

### Supported Levels

- **`context`**: Focuses on a `system` and its interactions with `actor`s and `external-system`s.
- **`container`**: Zooms into a `system` to show its constituent `container`s and external connections.
- **`component`**: Zooms into a `container` to reveal internal `component`s and dependencies.
- **`code`**: Materializes the implementation surface as a structured Markdown table of `source-module` artifacts, file paths, languages, and requirements implemented.
- **`deployment`**: Focuses on a `deployment-node`, showing nested nodes and the artifacts `deployed-on` it.
- **`dynamic`**: Focuses on a `system` and draws its ordered runtime interactions as a numbered sequence (Mermaid `C4Dynamic`, a PlantUML sequence diagram, a Structurizr `dynamic` view, or a D2 sequence diagram).

### Multiple Diagramming Backends

Quarto-Needs supports multiple diagramming backends via the `backend` argument:

```markdown
{{< need-c4 root="SYS-APP" level="container" backend="mermaid" >}}
{{< need-c4 root="SYS-APP" level="container" backend="plantuml" >}}
{{< need-c4 root="SYS-APP" level="container" backend="structurizr" >}}
{{< need-c4 root="SYS-APP" level="container" backend="d2" >}}
```

- **`mermaid`** (default): Embedded directly in HTML as responsive inline SVG.
- **`plantuml`**, **`structurizr`**, **`d2`**: If the respective tool is installed locally, pre-renders SVG/PNG assets; otherwise falls back gracefully to syntax-highlighted diagram source code.

Deployment-level PlantUML output includes the `C4_Deployment` stdlib; a PlantUML old enough to lack that file falls back to source text exactly like a missing backend.

Because that fallback is silent, a publishing pipeline can ship source code where diagrams belong. Run `tools/install_diagram_backends.sh` to provision all three on Linux; CI runs the same script and then fails the build if any diagram rendered as source.

## Architecture Governance (C4 Rules)

The C4 rule engine validates diagram structural integrity:

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| `C4001` | In a Container view, every container must declare its parent system via `part-of` |
| `C4002` | In a Component view, every component must declare its parent container via `part-of` |
| `C4003` | Inter-element relations must have a descriptive label |
| `C4004` | Hierarchy violations (e.g. cyclic containment or orphan boundaries) are rejected |
